item: A paged article browse asks for ids first and excludes quarantined rows through the covering index, so it reads only the rows it shows
status: shipped (plans measured; times from the 2026-10-06 synthetic 2 GB store; awaiting the operator's next bundle)
summary: The article-list browse selected whole Article rows and tested quarantined IS NOT 1, which no index answers, so every row a scan stepped over or an OFFSET skipped was read with its body. A paged browse now selects ids (ordered and cut by the database), loads the page's rows by id (chunked under the bound-parameter limit), and excludes quarantined rows with id NOT IN (the quarantined ids), answered by the covering quarantined index; the reader that includes quarantined items keeps the stand-in condition. Measured on a 40,000-article 2 GB synthetic store, cold cache: a page 20,000 rows deep 720 to 34 ms, a sort by source 944 to 40 ms, the first page unchanged. With the language and title indexes the language filter and the title sort page statements are answered from their index (plan tests pin it; no new time measured).
